hero.title: Toll Brothers Digital Studio
hero.subtitle: I designed four home customization tools for the Toll Brothers Studio app that replaced 30+ PDFs.

blocks.text: Home customization is a major part of the Toll Brothers brand, and that process traditionally relied on outdated digital modules and PDFs. The Digital Studio app is a new initiative to create a comprehensive digital experience for home customization. I led end-to-end design on four major modules for the Digital Studio. For homebuyers, I designed the Floorplan Configurator, the Furniture Planner, and Digital Catalog. For our internal product teams, I designed the Collection Builder to feed curated sets into the Digital Catalog.
Floorplan customization relied on an old Floorplan Configurator built by a third party vendor. The old module had major design flaws.

figures.caption: Many options have complex constraint logic (e.g., selecting Option A disables Option B), but the UI fails to communicate it.
Users have to rely on trial-and-error and dense tooltips, resulting in a frustrating experience.
It’s built on desktop-first principles. On mobile, it lacks features and has wonky controls.

blocks.text: To design a better solution, I researched 80 home designs that offer floorplan customization to understand the full scope of constraints. Then, I established a proper framework with three basic buckets.

items: Independent - Options that can be toggled independently of any other options.
Child - Options that can be toggled on if another independent option is toggled on.
Mutual Exclusion - A group of 2+ options where only one option can be selected.
Partial Conflict Group - A group of 3+ options where some options have asymmetric internal conflicts.

blocks.subtitle: Design
blocks.text: In order to redesign the experience around mobile-first principles, I picked the popular bottom sheet pattern that can dynamically alter size based on current focus. I then redesigned the list and demonstrated to stakeholders the framework for categorizing and visualizing dependencies. My manager and an Architecture Product Manager approved the framework and the overall redesign.

On the internal product side, the product team would curate features for designer-appointed collections using PDFs. As the company pivoted to more pre-selected builds and quick move-in homes, the product team needed an internal tool to construct collections of products at scale. I partnered with a senior developer and designed the MVP wireframes from scratch. For a desktop-only tool, these were the basic requirements:

items: Upload new features to the system.

figures.caption: Collection Builder main page showing collection cards with mosaic feature thumbnails. Cards are categorized by publish states.

A single collection showing added features categorized by location. A general Select Features button is in the top-right corner, and each location has a smaller location-specific Select Features button.
Select Features shows selected and recommended features. The gray indicator in the top-right corner communicates selection state and enables location changes.
The Upload Feature appears as a tab in Select Features. Product teams can upload spreadsheets of features. There are duplication guardrails.

blocks.text: During the build process, my developer partner and I fleshed out additional management-focused requirements, such as multi-upload, duplicate prevention, and publish states. The demo for this project received internal approval and was added to the backlog.

I revisited the Design Your Own Home module to add a mobile-optimized furniture planner function. The old design includes a furniture planner available only on desktop. To elegantly add a furniture planner to mobile, I reduced its prominence, added a variant-selection state, and removed resizing features that do not apply to furniture with preset sizes.

figures.caption: The furniture planner button is placed in the bottom-right corner.
Users can select from a horizontal carousel of furniture categories.
Users can place a default piece and then move, rotate, delete, or change variants.
Users can swap furniture variants in a dedicated variant-swap state.

blocks.text: The digital catalog is an ongoing team effort to replace PDF catalogs with a digital app experience. Users take a style survey, receive a recommended curated set of finishes, and adjust the selection. I designed several key screens with feature scalability in mind, creating a reusable selection pattern for cabinets that can be repurposed for other features like flooring.

figures.caption: Style Survey prefills the majority of hardware and finishes. The flow is optimized for refinement over selection.
The Cabinet tab in the Kitchen selection flow balances several required elements: navigation, visualizer, stacked cabinet toggle, zoning, filters, selection, return option, and confirmation bar.
Flooring exists as its own section, allowing users to compare kitchen and bath flooring, and accommodating grout selection.
Grout selection expands the bottom confirmation bar into a full bottom sheet.
